title: GPS3-E/H: GPS with the Pell leading coefficient a > 1/sqrt 2 (stacked envelopes), O(n^2) bits, O(n) qubits, heralded tolerance 1-1/(10^64-3)^4

claims.statement: For every integer N >= 2 and every s in Z/NZ, with n = ceil(log2 N), L = log2 n and t = sqrt(n log2 n), the single GPS algorithm and complete parameter rule of proof.md (width profile, Grover pair search, acquisition cutoff Qcap and weighted-attempt cutoff Wcap), with every source acquisition on both branches served by the heralded filter FILTER of heralded.md (the identity when copies carry no herald; literal raw-acquisition cutoff D Q*, D = (10^64-3)^4, Q* the literal handed-over sample cap of heralded.md H.2, namely N(n+10) for n < 256 and Qcap for n >= 256; the acquisition counter, Qcap and the EXTRACT parameter h of proof.md count handed-over copies; heralded.md Lemmas H.1-H.2 and Theorem H.3), recovers the entire s with unconditional probability at least 1-2^-8 > 3/4 for the clean problem (independent ideal source copies) and for every adversary of the heralded malformed-copy model of the fifth claim. On EVERY execution branch, including all retries, discarded copies, failed attempts, both cutoff branches, FILTER's raw acquisitions, herald reads, resets, counter steps and its raw cutoff, its total charged sequential work obeys T(N,s) = O(n^5 (log2 n)^2 2^R) (proof.md Section 9.4 and heralded.md Theorem H.3: FILTER's extra work is O(D Q* n log n)), hence T(N,s) = O(E(n)), where E(n) = 2^(a t - K sum_(j=1..M) n^(1/2) (log2 n)^(q_j)) with a = p/q = , the exact Pell rational with 2p^2 - q^2 = 1 (so a > 1/sqrt 2), gcd(p,q) = 1 and 140 p < 99 q (so a < 99/140), K = 10^256 - 1, M = 19, q_j = 1/2 - 1/(2 e_j) and e_j = 10^256 - (2j-1) for j = 1, ..., M (the structured object lists E term by term, every rational in lowest terms). This follows from the threshold Lemma 9.2 of proof.md applied with the rational c' = a - 1/(10 q^2), which satisfies 1/sqrt 2 < c' < a by exact integer inequalities (proof.md Section 9.6), giving R <= c' t + 1 for all n >= 2^(L0(c')) with R = R(n) the profile parameter of proof.md Section 4.1 (the least integer R >= 2 with S(R) >= n - 1), the finitely many smaller bit lengths being covered by the absolute outer constant, and from the absorption Lemma 9.6 of proof.md (n^P (log2 n)^P' 2^(c' t) = O(E(n)) for all fixed P, P', using only a - c' > 0; its threshold is astronomically large and only its existence is used). The uniform bit-length envelope is B_T(n) = E(n) for n >= 2, with the explicit finite branch covering all smaller cases. Its exact growth index is 1/2. All outside constants are absolute and independent of N, s and outcomes, and this bound holds jointly with the other three resource bounds and the heralded fractional-tolerance claim for this same algorithm/configuration.

For the same GPS algorithm and complete parameter rule as all four resource claims of proof.md, with every source acquisition on both branches served by the heralded filter FILTER of heralded.md (the identity when copies carry no herald; literal raw-acquisition cutoff D Q*, D = (10^64-3)^4, Q* the literal handed-over sample cap of heralded.md H.2, namely N(n+10) for n < 256 and Qcap for n >= 256; the acquisition counter, Qcap and the EXTRACT parameter h of proof.md count handed-over copies; heralded.md Lemmas H.1-H.2 and Theorem H.3), the proved fractional error tolerance is epsilon(n) = 9999999999999999999999999999999999999999999999999999999999999996*9999999999999999999999999999999999999999999999999999999999999998*5909009547859618446014307935656485996455360061473289284034355157*8461654968574415353741992088106541809421651544931744139485636465*2/9999999999999999999999999999999999999999999999999999999999999997^4 = 1 - 1/x^4 with x = 10^64 - 3, a constant in (0,1), valid for every N >= 2, under the heralded malformed-copy model stated in error_model; the displayed integers of heralded.md H.6 multiply to x^2 + 1. If at most floor(epsilon(n) Q') of the Q' raw acquired copies are malformed on every branch, then for every N >= 2 and every s in Z/NZ the output equals the entire s with probability at least 1-2^-8 > 3/4, jointly with the four resource bounds of claims 0-3 on every execution branch (heralded.md Lemmas H.1-H.2 and Theorem H.3, using the clean-problem success proof of proof.md Section 8). With no herald (the clean problem) the algorithm is exactly GPS3 of proof.md. The clean-copy tolerance 0 of the source remains proved in proof.md but is not claimed here. No tolerance of undetectable corruption and no impossibility of greater tolerance is claimed.

structured.error_model: Heralded malformed-copy model with fraction epsilon(n). Parameters: N >= 2 is the modulus, s in Z/NZ the secret, n = ceil(log2 N), Q the total number of source copies the algorithm acquires on an execution branch, and epsilon(n) the tolerated malformed fraction. Each acquired copy consists of an (n+1)-qubit register of the ideal copy's shape together with one classical herald bit f delivered with it. Copies are delivered one at a time in acquisition order j = 1, ..., Q. Before copy j is delivered, an adversary that knows N, s, the full description of the algorithm and every measurement outcome the algorithm obtained before copy j is delivered, and that may hold, process and measure an arbitrary private quantum system, decides adaptively whether copy j is malformed. A well-formed copy has f = 0 and its register is a fresh copy of rho_s, in tensor product with every other system (earlier copies, the adversary's system and the algorithm's registers). A malformed copy has f = 1 and its register is in an arbitrary state chosen by the adversary, possibly entangled with the adversary's private system and with other malformed copies. On every execution branch at most floor(epsilon(n) Q) of the Q acquired copies are malformed. The herald is always correct, so malformation is detectable (an erasure-type error); its timing, its number within the promise and the malformed register contents are adversarial. In the clean problem no herald is supplied and every copy is well-formed. No source control, purification access or preparation inverse is supplied.
